paper.title_en: Chiral bosonic mean-field Ansatz and spin dynamics in spin-1 Kitaev magnets
paper.abstract_en: The Kitaev model is a paradigmatic system for realizing quantum spin liquids, but its higher-spin extensions are not exactly solvable, and their spin dynamics is less well understood than in the spin-$1/2$ case. We reexamine a previously introduced triplet-pairing $φ_t=π/2$ phase pattern for the antiferromagnetic $S=1$ Kitaev model and extend the analysis to weak symmetric off-diagonal exchanges $Γ$ and $Γ'$. Using a bond-operator formulation of Schwinger-boson mean-field theory, we calculate the dynamical spin structure factor for the triplet $0$-flux and $π/2$-flux states. At the pure Kitaev point, the $π/2$-flux Ansatz yields a flatter spectrum, consistent with its weakly dispersive spinon bands, and suppresses longer-range spin correlations more strongly than the $0$-flux Ansatz. Spectral flatness provides a consistency check for short-ranged spin correlations but is not, by itself, a diagnostic of time-reversal symmetry breaking. Three-spin correlations reveal staggered chirality in the mean-field state, which breaks time reversal but preserves combined inversion and time reversal. At the pure Kitaev point, the $π/2$-flux Ansatz also captures the dominant low-energy features of the exact-diagonalization spectra better than the $0$-flux Ansatz. For representative weak perturbations along $Γ'=Γ$, we obtain gapped solutions within the constrained $π/2$-flux manifold. These results support the triplet $π/2$-flux chiral bosonic Ansatz as a useful mean-field description of spin dynamics near the antiferromagnetic $S=1$ Kitaev limit with weak off-diagonal exchanges.
